analysis.title: eToro Group (ETOR): First take: Slightly better adj. expenses, but weaker ECC quarterly results, and October run rate
key_insights: ETOR reported 3Q26 EPS of 14c, below GSe/Visible Alpha consensus of 27c/23c. Adj. EPS (ex. SBC) was 26c, below GSe/consensus of 33c/29c.

GS expects a muted reaction. Slightly better adjusted expenses are likely to be outweighed by weaker net contribution (weaker ECC, partly offset by stronger Crypto, both vs. the Street) and lower October-implied 4Q26E ECC and crypto trends than GSe/consensus.
Net contribution came in 1% below the Street: eToro Money -13%, ECC -11%, Subscription & other -42%, partly offset by Crypto +85% and net interest +2%. Adj. expenses were 1% below the Street.
Adj. pre-tax margin was 17.3%, about 35bps below Street estimates and down about 16.7pp QoQ.

3Q26 ECC revenue per trade was $0.60 vs GSe/Street $0.67/$0.64. Crypto take rate was 1.87% vs GSe/Street 0.90%/0.89%. Much of the sequential crypto increase may reflect positive crypto mark to market, about $5.3mn on ~$13mn of corporate crypto treasury holdings and 41% crypto market cap appreciation.
Run-rating October ECC trades for the full quarter implies 140mn trades, 19%/18% below the 4Q26 Street/GSe of 172mn/170mn and down about 5% QoQ.
Run-rating October crypto volumes implies $1.3bn, below 4Q26 consensus/GSe of $2.0bn/$1.7bn and down 8% QoQ.

October funded accounts were 4.42mn, growing 8% MoM annualized and up 18% YoY (+10% YoY adjusted for Zengo, Bit2C and Spaceship), vs management guidance of double-digit annual funded account growth over time. Net new accounts were 30k in each of September and October.

ETOR announced the acquisition of LB Finanzas, a digital investment and payment platform in Argentina. The metrics of the TradeZero acquisition announced at 2Q26 results were previously not disclosed.

GS wants clarity on drivers of weaker October/3Q26 ECC volume and the retail trading outlook, LB Finanzas and TradeZero customer base and revenue contribution, ECC take rates, and near-term crypto volume trends.
GS rates ETOR Neutral with a $29 12-month price target, based on 7.0x P/E on Q5-Q8 EPS ex SBC. Price was $23.32 at the 9 Nov 2026 close, implying 24.4% upside.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral rating and $29 target maintained after the 3Q26 print. Results missed on EPS and October run-rate trends were below consensus, while expenses were slightly better.

earnings_insights: ETOR 3Q26 reported EPS 14c vs GSe 27c and Visible Alpha consensus 23c (reported 11/10/2026 release, estimates are GSe/consensus).
ETOR 3Q26 adj. EPS ex-SBC 26c vs GSe 33c and consensus 29c. GS calculates consensus EPS from consensus P&L components rather than the data provider's EPS estimate.
3Q26 ECC net contribution $88.5mn, down 38% QoQ and 11% below the Street, with net trading contribution per trade 7% lower and ECC trades 4% lower vs. the Street.
3Q26 Crypto net contribution $26.3mn, up 139% QoQ and 85% above consensus, with a take rate 96bps above the Street and volumes 11% below.

3Q26 net interest contribution $50mn, up 2% QoQ and 2% above the Street, on NIM 9bps higher and average earning assets 1% lower vs. the Street. Interest earning assets were $7.0bn at 3Q26 vs $7.9bn at 3Q25.
3Q26 eToro Money contribution $20mn, down 23% QoQ and 13% below consensus, on a 3bps lower effective fee rate and 9% lower total money transfers.
Adj. total expenses were 1% below the Street, driven by 11% lower G&A vs. the Street.
GS estimates EPS of $0.33 for 9/26E, $0.61 for 12/26E and $0.70 for 3/27E. FY EPS estimates are $2.55 for 2026E, $3.59 for 2027E and $4.37 for 2028E.
crypto_views: ETOR crypto net contribution of $26.3mn rose 139% QoQ and was 85% above consensus, helped by a 1.87% take rate, though some of the increase may reflect crypto mark-to-market gains on corporate treasury holdings.
September/October crypto trades were 2.4mn/2.0mn, down 55%/17% MoM. Run-rated October crypto volume implies $1.3bn for 4Q26, below consensus $2.0bn and GSe $1.7bn.
risk_factors: Downside risks: unsuccessful US expansion, retail trading cycle slows down, crypto market enters a downturn, substantially lower interest rates.
Upside risks: US expansion happens more quickly and cheaply, CopyTrader is more differentiated and harder to replicate than expected, crypto trading accelerates once again.
October funded account growth of 8% MoM annualized is below management's double-digit growth guidance.
